To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of an ATM LAN depends on the output link scheduling policy of its switches, and that the performance of different output link scheduling policies depends on the deadlines of the real-time messages.
the performance of ATM switches is highly sensitive to the output link scheduling policy.
the admission probability metric is an effective tool for evaluating the performance of admission policies for ATM LANs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of connection admission control in an ATM based real-time communication system.
the problem of designing an ATM LAN to support real-time applications.
the problem of admission control in an ATM LAN with real-time connections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FCFS is the best choice for real-time scheduling in ATM LANs.
the PGPS policy performs better than the FCFS and RR policies in terms of the admission probability, but the FCFS policy performs better than PGPS and RR in terms of the average packet delay.
the scheduling policy should be selected based on the application requirements and the available resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the output link scheduling policy can have a significant effect on the ability of the network to support real-time connections.
we have developed a framework to evaluate the performance of ATM LANs for real-time applications.
the performance of an ATM switch in an embedded real-time system is determined by the scheduling discipline of the output link of the ATM switch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple scheduling policy like RR can be as good as a complex policy like PGPS, if the deadlines of the connections are large.
the output link scheduling policies of an ATM switch can significantly affect its performance.
the output link scheduling policy of a switch can have a profound effect on the ability of the network to support real-time traffic.
